key_insight: Mac-Diff is a conditional diffusion model that uses locality-aware cross-modal attention to generate diverse, realistic conformational ensembles for unseen proteins, capturing both dynamic flexibility and structural heterogeneity in a single generative framework.
problem_solved: Existing generative and prediction methods often produce single static structures or fail to capture realistic ensemble diversity and local structural correlations; this work addresses how to model and generate diverse, physically plausible protein conformations for proteins not seen during training.
method: Conditional diffusion backbone that generates 3D protein conformations conditioned on sequence and/or template information.
Locality-aware modal alignment: cross-modal attention that emphasizes local structural neighborhoods to align sequence/feature modalities with spatial geometry.
Ensemble-focused training and sampling strategies to encourage multimodal outputs reflecting realistic flexibility and heterogeneity.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners with a generative framework to produce diverse, physically meaningful protein ensembles, enabling downstream tasks (dynamics analysis, drug design, uncertainty estimation) that require structural variability rather than a single static prediction.
visual_elements: Model schematic: conditional diffusion pipeline with a highlighted locality-aware cross-modal attention module.
Before/after overlay: multiple predicted conformers of the same protein vs single-structure baseline (transparent ribbon overlays).
Diversity metrics chart: RMSD distribution or ensemble spread comparison between Mac-Diff and baselines.
Attention map example: heatmap showing locality-focused cross-modal alignment on a protein fragment.
paper_title: Conditional diffusion with locality-aware modal alignment for generating diverse protein conformational ensembles
paper_authors: Baoli Wang, Chenglin Wang, Jingyang Chen, Danlin Liu, Changzhi Sun
